interview.contentItem.audioLabel.description: Accessible name of an audio player in protocol content that the researcher has not described.

interview.contentItem.videoLabel.description: Accessible name of a video player in protocol content that the researcher has not described.

interview.familyPedigree.actionsLabel.defaultMessage: {isYou, select, true {Add your relatives} other {Add relatives of {name}}}
interview.familyPedigree.actionsLabel.description: Accessible name of the group of buttons that appears around a selected family member, used to add their parent, sibling, partner or child.

interview.familyPedigree.addedAnnounceme.description: Screen reader announcement after a family member is added. {name} is their name or, when it is not known, how they are related to the participant.

interview.familyPedigree.canvasLabel.description: Accessible name for the area showing the family members the participant has added, drawn as a family tree.

interview.familyPedigree.childrenAnswere.defaultMessage: {isYou, select, true {Recorded that you have no biological children.} other {Recorded that {name} has no biological children.}}
interview.familyPedigree.childrenAnswere.description: Screen reader announcement after answering, from the list of family members still needed, that a person has no children. name is the person’s name or how they are related to the participant.

interview.familyPedigree.connectHint.defaultMessage: Select a person, then select another to connect them.
interview.familyPedigree.connectHint.description: Shown over the family tree while the Connect tool is chosen, telling the participant how to join two people already in the tree.

interview.familyPedigree.connectHintLink.defaultMessage: {isYou, select, true {Now select the person to connect to you.} other {Now select the person to connect to {name}.}}
interview.familyPedigree.connectHintLink.description: Read out to screen reader users, not shown, once the first of two people to connect has been selected. name is that person’s name or how they are related to the participant.

interview.familyPedigree.connectTool.description: Name of the family tree toolbar tool that joins two people already in the tree with a relationship. Shown as the tool’s tooltip heading and read as its accessible name.

interview.familyPedigree.connectToolDesc.defaultMessage: Select two family members to connect them and say how they are related.
interview.familyPedigree.connectToolDesc.description: Tooltip text, under the heading “Connect” (or the stage’s own name for it), of the family tree toolbar tool that joins two people already in the tree: the participant selects one, then another, then chooses how they are related, such as parent or partner. Read by participants.

interview.familyPedigree.connectedParent.description: Screen reader announcement after connecting two people as parent and child. relationship is the chosen menu option (for example Julie is a parent of Rob); kind is the kind of parent chosen (for example Adoptive parent).

interview.familyPedigree.disconnectHint.defaultMessage: Select a person, then select someone they are connected to, to remove that connection.
interview.familyPedigree.disconnectHint.description: Shown over the family tree while the Disconnect tool is chosen, telling the participant how to remove a relationship line.

interview.familyPedigree.disconnectHintL.defaultMessage: {isYou, select, true {Now select the person to disconnect from you.} other {Now select the person to disconnect from {name}.}}
interview.familyPedigree.disconnectHintL.description: Read out to screen reader users, not shown, once the first of two people to disconnect has been selected. name is that person’s name or how they are related to the participant.

interview.familyPedigree.disconnectTool.description: Name of the family tree toolbar tool that removes a relationship line between two people. Shown as the tool’s tooltip heading and read as its accessible name.

interview.familyPedigree.disconnectToolD.defaultMessage: Select two connected family members to remove the connection between them.
interview.familyPedigree.disconnectToolD.description: Tooltip text, under the heading “Disconnect” (or the stage’s own name for it), of the family tree toolbar tool that removes a relationship line: the participant selects one person, then someone they are connected to, and confirms. Read by participants.

interview.familyPedigree.disconnectedAnn.defaultMessage: {firstIsYou, select, true {The connection between you and {second} was removed.} other {The connection between {first} and {second} was removed.}}
interview.familyPedigree.disconnectedAnn.description: Screen reader announcement after the connection between two people is removed. first and second are their names or how they are related to the participant.

interview.familyPedigree.framingChoiceDe.defaultMessage: Choose the words you would like us to use for the people in your family. You can change this at any time.
interview.familyPedigree.framingChoiceDe.description: Explanation under the question asking which set of words for relatives the family tree should use.

interview.familyPedigree.framingChoiceTi.defaultMessage: How should we describe your family?
interview.familyPedigree.framingChoiceTi.description: Question over the choice between sets of words for relatives, such as mother and father, or egg parent and sperm parent.

interview.familyPedigree.framingChosenAn.defaultMessage: {framing, select, gamete {Family members are now described with words like egg parent, sperm parent and sibling.} other {Family members are now described with words like mother, father, sister and brother.}}
interview.familyPedigree.framingChosenAn.description: Screen-reader announcement after the participant chooses the words used to describe family members, which changes the labels of everyone they have not named. {framing} is "gamete" for the words that do not depend on gender, otherwise the words that follow gender.

interview.familyPedigree.framingControlD.defaultMessage: Choose the relationship words your family tree uses for your relatives.
interview.familyPedigree.framingControlD.description: Tooltip text, under the heading “Wording” (or the stage’s own name for it), of the family tree toolbar button that opens a choice between sets of words for relatives, such as mother and father, or egg parent and sperm parent. Read by participants.

interview.familyPedigree.framingControlL.description: Name of the family tree toolbar button that opens a choice between sets of words for relatives, such as mother and father, or egg parent and sperm parent. Shown as its tooltip heading and read as its accessible name.

interview.familyPedigree.personAccessibl.description: Accessible name of a family member’s symbol in the family tree. {name} is the person’s name, exactly as the participant typed it, or, when it is not known, how they are related to the participant.

interview.familyPedigree.personAdoptedDe.description: Read out after the name of a family member’s symbol in the family tree when the person was adopted, which the tree shows by drawing brackets around their symbol.

interview.familyPedigree.personMissingDe.description: Read out after the name of a family member’s symbol in the family tree when required details about the person have not been given yet, which the tree shows with a warning icon.

interview.familyPedigree.pointerTool.description: Name of the family tree toolbar tool that is chosen by default: with it, selecting a family member opens their details, and buttons beside them add a parent, sibling, partner or child. Shown as the tool’s tooltip heading and read as its accessible name.

interview.familyPedigree.pointerToolDesc.defaultMessage: Select a family member to edit their details or add their relatives.
interview.familyPedigree.pointerToolDesc.description: Tooltip text, under the heading “Add and edit” (or the stage’s own name for it), of the family tree toolbar tool that is chosen by default: with it, selecting a family member opens their details, and buttons beside them add a parent, sibling, partner or child. Read by participants.

interview.familyPedigree.redoDescription.defaultMessage: Bring back the change you undid.
interview.familyPedigree.redoDescription.description: Tooltip text, under the heading “Redo”, of the family tree toolbar button that makes again a change to the family tree that Undo reversed. Read by participants.

interview.familyPedigree.redoneAnnouncem.description: Screen reader announcement after the participant redoes a change to the family tree they had undone.

interview.familyPedigree.removedAnnounce.description: Screen reader announcement after a family member is removed. {name} is their name or, when it is not known, how they are related to the participant.

interview.familyPedigree.removedWithOthe.defaultMessage: {count, plural, one {{name} and one other person removed from your family.} other {{name} and # other people removed from your family.}}
interview.familyPedigree.removedWithOthe.description: Screen reader announcement after a family member is removed along with the people who were connected to the participant only through them. {name} is the name of the person the participant chose to remove or, when it is not known, how they are related to the participant; count is how many other people were removed with them.

interview.familyPedigree.reproductiveRol.defaultMessage: {role, select, donor {egg or sperm donor} traditionalSurrogate {egg donor who carried the pregnancy} other {surrogate}}
interview.familyPedigree.reproductiveRol.description: Read out with a family member’s symbol in the family tree, for each part they played in someone else’s conception or birth (the tree draws no mark for these). "donor" is someone who donated an egg or sperm; "traditionalSurrogate" is an egg donor who also carried the pregnancy; "other" is a surrogate who carried the pregnancy without a genetic tie to the child. When someone has more than one role, the phrases are joined into a list, so write each as it would appear inside a sentence (lower case in English).

interview.familyPedigree.savedAnnounceme.description: Screen reader announcement after a family member’s details are saved.

interview.familyPedigree.showWholeFamily.description: Accessible name of the toolbar icon button that zooms and moves the family tree so everyone in it fits on screen. Also the heading of the button’s tooltip.

interview.familyPedigree.showWholeFamily.defaultMessage: Fit your whole family tree on the screen.
interview.familyPedigree.showWholeFamily.description: Tooltip text, under the heading “Show the whole family”, of the toolbar icon button that zooms and moves the family tree so everyone in it fits on screen. Read by participants.

interview.familyPedigree.siblingsAnswere.defaultMessage: {isYou, select, true {Recorded that you have no biological brothers or sisters.} other {Recorded that {name} has no biological brothers or sisters.}}
interview.familyPedigree.siblingsAnswere.description: Screen reader announcement after answering, from the list of family members still needed, that a person has no siblings. name is the person’s name or how they are related to the participant.

interview.familyPedigree.skipStep.description: Button in the side panel where a new family member’s details are given, one group of questions at a time. Shown while some questions in the group are left unanswered; it moves on to the next group without answering them. They can still be answered by going back.

interview.familyPedigree.toolGroupLabel.description: Accessible name of the pair of buttons in the toolbar that choose what selecting a person does.

interview.familyPedigree.toolsLabel.description: Accessible name of the toolbar above the family tree, which switches between adding or editing people, connecting two people, and removing the connection between two people.

interview.familyPedigree.trackerAllDetai.defaultMessage: Add required details for all family members
interview.familyPedigree.trackerAllDetai.description: An item at the end of the family tree’s progress list, read by the participant, standing for the details the researcher requires of every person in the family (such as sex assigned at birth). It is shown while nobody already in the family is missing any, as a plain item while other relatives still have to be added, and ticked and struck through once nothing else is needed. While some are missing, the list instead names each person whose details are missing.

interview.familyPedigree.trackerItemDone.description: Read out by screen readers before an item in the family tree’s progress list that is already done, which is shown ticked and struck through. The item follows, for example “Add your parents”.

interview.familyPedigree.trackerProgress.defaultMessage: {complete, select, true {Your family tree has everything needed} other {Family tree {percent, number, percent} complete}}. Show what’s still needed.
interview.familyPedigree.trackerProgress.description: Accessible name of the round progress indicator in the corner of the family tree, which opens the list of family members still needed. percent is a fraction between 0 and 1.

interview.familyPedigree.undoDescription.defaultMessage: Undo your last change to your family tree.
interview.familyPedigree.undoDescription.description: Tooltip text, under the heading “Undo”, of the family tree toolbar button that reverses the most recent change: adding, editing or removing a family member, connecting or disconnecting two people, or selecting someone for a question. Read by participants.

interview.familyPedigree.undoneAnnouncem.description: Screen reader announcement after the participant undoes their most recent change to the family tree.

interview.familyPedigree.viewToolsLabel.description: Accessible name of the small toolbar beside the family tree tools that zooms the family tree out and in, and fits the whole family on the screen.

interview.familyPedigree.zoomInDescripti.defaultMessage: Make your family tree bigger, to see part of it more closely.
interview.familyPedigree.zoomInDescripti.description: Tooltip text, under the heading “Zoom in”, of the family tree toolbar button that increases magnification. Read by participants.

interview.familyPedigree.zoomOutDescript.defaultMessage: Make your family tree smaller, to see more of it at once.
interview.familyPedigree.zoomOutDescript.description: Tooltip text, under the heading “Zoom out”, of the family tree toolbar button that decreases magnification. Read by participants.

interview.interfaceText.buttons.cancel.description: Generic action that abandons the current operation.

interview.interfaceText.buttons.delete.description: Generic action that removes the selected item.

interview.interfaceText.buttons.done.description: Generic action that finishes the current flow.

interview.interfaceText.buttons.no.description: Default negative option of a yes/no field.

interview.interfaceText.buttons.save.description: Generic action that persists the current changes.

interview.interfaceText.buttons.yes.description: The Yes answer to a yes-or-no question, and the button that confirms discarding a form’s unsaved changes when the participant leaves it.

interview.interfaceText.messages.error.description: Generic failure sentence shown when no more specific error applies, including when a form could not be submitted.

interview.interfaceText.messages.loading.description: Generic indicator shown while content is being fetched.

interview.interfaceText.navigation.back.description: Generic action that returns to the previous step.

interview.interfaceText.navigation.conti.description: Generic action that advances to the next step.

interview.interfaceText.passphrase.passw.description: Default placeholder of a password input.

interview.interfaceText.search.searchLab.description: Label, accessible name and placeholder of a search box: the one that filters the interview’s list of screens, and the one over a list of people to choose from.

interview.interfaceText.validation.diffe.defaultMessage: {hasLabel, select, true {Your answer must be different from your answer to ''{label}''.} other {Your answer must be different from your earlier answer.}}
interview.interfaceText.validation.diffe.description: Error and hint for a must-differ comparison. hasLabel says whether the other question has a visible label; label is that label.

interview.interfaceText.validation.great.defaultMessage: {hasLabel, select, true {Your answer must be greater than your answer to ''{label}''.} other {Your answer must be greater than your earlier answer.}}
interview.interfaceText.validation.great.description: Error and hint for a must-be-greater comparison. hasLabel says whether the other question has a visible label; label is that label.

interview.interfaceText.validation.great.defaultMessage: {hasLabel, select, true {Your answer must be the same as or greater than your answer to ''{label}''.} other {Your answer must be the same as or greater than your earlier answer.}}
interview.interfaceText.validation.great.description: Error and hint for a must-be-at-least comparison. hasLabel says whether the other question has a visible label; label is that label.

interview.interfaceText.validation.lessT.defaultMessage: {hasLabel, select, true {Your answer must be less than your answer to ''{label}''.} other {Your answer must be less than your earlier answer.}}
interview.interfaceText.validation.lessT.description: Error and hint for a must-be-less comparison. hasLabel says whether the other question has a visible label; label is that label.

interview.interfaceText.validation.lessT.defaultMessage: {hasLabel, select, true {Your answer must be the same as or less than your answer to ''{label}''.} other {Your answer must be the same as or less than your earlier answer.}}
interview.interfaceText.validation.lessT.description: Error and hint for a must-be-at-most comparison. hasLabel says whether the other question has a visible label; label is that label.

interview.interfaceText.validation.maxDa.description: Hint and error for a date/time maximum; {max} is the formatted bound.

interview.interfaceText.validation.maxLe.defaultMessage: {max, plural, one {Enter at most # character.} other {Enter at most # characters.}}
interview.interfaceText.validation.maxLe.description: Error and hint shown when text is longer than its maximum length.

interview.interfaceText.validation.maxSe.defaultMessage: {count, plural, one {Select a maximum of # value.} other {Select a maximum of # values.}}
interview.interfaceText.validation.maxSe.description: Error and hint shown when too many options are selected.

interview.interfaceText.validation.maxVa.defaultMessage: Enter a value less than or equal to {max}.
interview.interfaceText.validation.maxVa.description: Error and hint shown when a number is above its maximum.

interview.interfaceText.validation.minDa.description: Hint and error for a date/time minimum; {min} is the formatted bound.

interview.interfaceText.validation.minLe.defaultMessage: {min, plural, one {Enter at least # character.} other {Enter at least # characters.}}
interview.interfaceText.validation.minLe.description: Error and hint shown when text is shorter than its minimum length.

interview.interfaceText.validation.minSe.defaultMessage: {count, plural, one {Select at least # value.} other {Select at least # values.}}
interview.interfaceText.validation.minSe.description: Error and hint shown when too few options are selected.

interview.interfaceText.validation.minVa.defaultMessage: Enter a value greater than or equal to {min}.
interview.interfaceText.validation.minVa.description: Error and hint shown when a number is below its minimum.

interview.interfaceText.validation.requi.defaultMessage: You must answer this question before continuing.
interview.interfaceText.validation.requi.description: Error shown when a required form field is left unanswered.

interview.interfaceText.validation.sameA.defaultMessage: {hasLabel, select, true {Your answer must be the same as your answer to ''{label}''.} other {Your answer must be the same as your earlier answer.}}
interview.interfaceText.validation.sameA.description: Error and hint for a must-match comparison. hasLabel says whether the other question has a visible label; label is that label.

interview.interfaceText.validation.uniqu.description: Error and hint shown when a value duplicates one used elsewhere.

interview.interfaces.addNamePlaceholder.defaultMessage: Type a name, then press Enter
interview.interfaces.addNamePlaceholder.description: Placeholder in the network-composer name field; pressing Enter adds the named item.

interview.interfaces.addedNodes.description: Accessible name used by drag-and-drop announcements for the list of people already added to the network.

interview.interfaces.availableItems.defaultMessage: List of available items to add
interview.interfaces.availableItems.description: Accessible name of the collection containing external roster entries that can be added.

interview.interfaces.availableRosterNode.description: Accessible name used by drag-and-drop announcements for the external roster entries that can still be added.

interview.interfaces.binSelectComplete.description: Announced to screen readers on a sorting screen once everything the participant was sorting (usually people, but it can be places, organisations or anything else) has been put in a group.

interview.interfaces.binSelectInstructio.description: Announced to screen readers when the item a participant is placing changes, on a sorting screen that asks them to tap a group instead of dragging. Sighted participants see that item shown as selected. An item is whatever the researcher has the participant sort: usually a person, but it can be a place, an organisation or anything else. name is the item’s unchanged participant-entered or authored display name. The groups are researcher-authored and shown on the same screen.

interview.interfaces.binSelectPlaceHere.description: Button inside an opened group on a sorting screen that puts the item the participant is placing (usually a person) into that group.

interview.interfaces.binSelectPlaceIn.description: Accessible name of a group a participant taps to put an item (usually a person) in it. name is the item’s unchanged participant-entered or authored display name; label is the unchanged researcher-authored group label.

interview.interfaces.binSelectShowConten.defaultMessage: Show what is in {label}, {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}
interview.interfaces.binSelectShowConten.description: Accessible name of the small button on a group that opens it to show what is already in it. label is the unchanged researcher-authored group label; count is the number of items currently in the group.

interview.interfaces.categoryContents.defaultMessage: Category {label}, {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}
interview.interfaces.categoryContents.description: Accessible name of a collapsed category container. label is its authored category label; count is the number of items currently in the container.

interview.interfaces.categoryContentsExp.defaultMessage: Category {label}, {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}, expanded
interview.interfaces.categoryContentsExp.description: Accessible name of an expanded category container. label is its authored label; count is the number of items currently in it.

interview.interfaces.categoryDrop.description: Drag target announcement for a categorical response. label is the unchanged researcher-authored category label.

interview.interfaces.categoryList.description: Accessible name of the item list inside an expanded category. label is the unchanged researcher-authored category label.

interview.interfaces.clearSearch.description: Accessible action that clears the current geospatial search query.

interview.interfaces.closeSearch.description: Accessible name of the toggle while the geospatial place-search panel is open.

interview.interfaces.composerAddNode.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the network-composer tool that adds a node.

interview.interfaces.composerAutomaticLa.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the network-composer toggle that lays the nodes out automatically.

interview.interfaces.composerDrawEdge.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the network-composer tool that draws an edge between two nodes.

interview.interfaces.composerGroups.description: Name of the network-composer tool that puts nodes in groups, shown in its tooltip and read as its accessible name.

interview.interfaces.composerRedo.description: Accessible name of the network composer toolbar button that makes again a change that was undone. The button shows only an icon and no tooltip, so only screen readers read this, and it stays in English whatever the interview language.

interview.interfaces.composerTools.description: Accessible name of the vertical toolbar used to create and edit a network.

interview.interfaces.composerUndo.description: Accessible name of the network composer toolbar button that reverses the most recent change. The button shows only an icon and no tooltip, so only screen readers read this, and it stays in English whatever the interview language.

interview.interfaces.confirmPassphrase.description: Label of the second anonymisation password field; this is confirmation of the passphrase, not a separate password.

interview.interfaces.deselect.description: Action that clears the current outside-map-area selection so the participant can choose another location.

interview.interfaces.discardChangesDescr.defaultMessage: Do you want to discard your changes?
interview.interfaces.discardChangesDescr.description: Question asked when leaving a form with invalid unsaved answers. Continuing resets the form, so its unsaved changes will be lost.

interview.interfaces.discardChangesTitle.description: Title of the warning shown when a participant tries to leave a form containing invalid unsaved answers.

interview.interfaces.dontKnow.description: Answer option a participant picks when they do not know the answer to a question about a family member, such as whether twins are identical.

interview.interfaces.dragToReposition.description: Accessible name of the handle that moves the floating narrative preset toolbar.

interview.interfaces.drawingControls.description: Accessible name of the narrative toolbar group for freehand annotations.

interview.interfaces.editingTools.description: Accessible name of the toolbar group for selection, adding people, creating connections, and group membership.

interview.interfaces.emptyValue.description: Shown in place of a roster detail that has no value: a blank field or an empty list. Replaces a bare dash so screen readers announce it.

interview.interfaces.errorHeading.description: Short heading above an external-list loading error. This heading intentionally has no final period.

interview.interfaces.externalDataError.defaultMessage: External data could not be loaded.
interview.interfaces.externalDataError.description: Shown under the error heading when a list of people from a file the study provides could not be loaded.

interview.interfaces.finishingInterview.description: Announced to screen readers, not shown, while an interview that ends without asking the participant is being finished and its answers saved; sighted participants see only a loading animation. It can take a few seconds on a slow connection.

interview.interfaces.groupMembershipOpti.description: Accessible name of the popover containing group membership choices in the network composer.

interview.interfaces.groupMembershipPeop.description: Accessible name of the controls that set group membership for the currently selected people.

interview.interfaces.hideInstructions.description: Accessible action that collapses the floating instructions panel above a network view.

interview.interfaces.historyTools.description: Accessible name of the toolbar group containing undo and redo actions.

interview.interfaces.layoutAndDrawing.description: Accessible name of the narrative toolbar for automatic positioning and freehand annotations.

interview.interfaces.layoutControls.description: Accessible name of the narrative toolbar group that pauses or resumes automatic positioning.

interview.interfaces.layoutTools.description: Accessible name of the network-composer toolbar group that controls automatic positioning.

interview.interfaces.mapMoveFailed.defaultMessage: Search could not be completed. Try again in a moment.
interview.interfaces.mapMoveFailed.description: Screen-reader announcement when the map could not be moved to the search result the participant chose. Only screen readers read it, so it stays in English whatever the interview language.

interview.interfaces.mapMoved.description: Screen-reader announcement after a selected search result moves the map. place is the unchanged place name returned by the map service.

interview.interfaces.mapOffline.defaultMessage: You are offline — the map will not load until you reconnect.
interview.interfaces.mapOffline.description: Notice over a Geospatial map while the device is offline and the map cannot load.

interview.interfaces.mapTitle.description: Accessible region name of the native Mapbox canvas in the geospatial interface.

interview.interfaces.mapUnavailable.defaultMessage: This can happen if your browser or device does not support the features the map requires (for example, WebGL). Try a different browser or device, or contact the study organizer. You may be able to continue your interview by selecting the next arrow.
interview.interfaces.mapUnavailable.description: Explanation shown when a Geospatial map cannot be drawn at all.

interview.interfaces.mapZoomIn.description: Accessible name of the Geospatial map button that increases magnification. The button shows only an icon, so only screen readers read this, and it stays in English whatever the interview language.

interview.interfaces.mapZoomOut.description: Accessible name of the Geospatial map button that decreases magnification. The button shows only an icon, so only screen readers read this, and it stays in English whatever the interview language.

interview.interfaces.mapboxHomepage.description: Accessible name of the native map logo link that opens the Mapbox homepage; preserve the Mapbox brand name.

interview.interfaces.namedReturnedToDraw.description: Screen-reader announcement after an item is returned to the unplaced-items panel. name is its unchanged participant-entered or authored display name.

interview.interfaces.nextPreset.description: Action that selects the next researcher-configured narrative view.

interview.interfaces.ordinalContainer.description: Drag-and-drop name of a rating container. label is the unchanged researcher-authored ordinal response label; keep it as a value, not a translation key.

interview.interfaces.overtakenEditNotice.defaultMessage: Undo or redo changed an answer while you were editing it, so your edit has not been saved. To keep your edit, change that answer again. If you continue, your edit will be lost.
interview.interfaces.overtakenEditNotice.description: Explanation in the Discard changes dialog shown as the interviewer leaves a network-composer form whose answer an undo or redo changed while they were editing it.

interview.interfaces.passphraseAccepted.description: Success message after the participant enters, on the anonymisation screen, the passphrase they chose earlier in the interview. Next refers to the interview navigation arrow.

interview.interfaces.pauseLayout.description: Tooltip and accessible name of the toggle that stops the people on a network diagram from moving into place by themselves.

interview.interfaces.presetNavigation.description: Accessible name of the toolbar group that switches between researcher-configured narrative views.

interview.interfaces.presets.description: Accessible name of the narrative toolbar for switching between researcher-configured network views.

interview.interfaces.previousPreset.description: Action that selects the previous researcher-configured narrative view.

interview.interfaces.quickAddHint.defaultMessage: Press Enter when you are finished.
interview.interfaces.quickAddHint.description: Tooltip that opens over the quick-add name field after about five seconds without typing, until the first name is added, telling the participant how to add what they typed.

interview.interfaces.quickAddInput.description: Accessible name of the active quick-add toggle while its name-entry field is open.

interview.interfaces.recenterMap.description: Accessible name of the map button that restores the researcher-configured starting center and zoom.

interview.interfaces.redo.description: Name of the family pedigree toolbar button that makes again a change that was undone, shown in its tooltip.

interview.interfaces.resetAnnotations.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the Narrative button that clears everything drawn on the canvas.

interview.interfaces.resizePanel.description: Accessible name of the draggable divider that changes the width of the network-composer editing panel.

interview.interfaces.resizePanels.defaultMessage: Resize panel and node list areas
interview.interfaces.resizePanels.description: Accessible name of the divider between the source panel and the list of added people; dragging or keyboard controls resize the two areas.

interview.interfaces.resumeLayout.description: Tooltip and accessible name of the toggle that lets the people on a network diagram move into place by themselves again.

interview.interfaces.returnedToDrawer.description: Screen-reader announcement after an item without a usable name is removed from the canvas and returned to the unplaced-items panel.

interview.interfaces.scrollForQuestions.description: Accessible name and announcement of the arrows at the bottom of a long personal-information form, which show that more questions are below the visible area. Only screen readers read it, so it stays in English whatever the interview language.

interview.interfaces.searchFailed.defaultMessage: Search could not be completed. Try again in a moment.
interview.interfaces.searchFailed.description: Notice under the Geospatial map search when a search could not run.

interview.interfaces.searchLocation.description: Accessible name of the toggle that opens the geospatial place-search panel.

interview.interfaces.searchSuggestions.description: Accessible name of the list of places returned by geospatial search, including its loading and empty states.

interview.interfaces.select.description: Network-composer tool that selects existing people or connections for editing.

interview.narrativePedigree.clearFocus.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the button that stops focusing the family tree on one person.

interview.narrativePedigree.keyHasCondit.description: Key row: what the filled symbol means. condition is the name of the condition the key shows, which the protocol may use.

interview.narrativePedigree.keyHeading.description: Heading over the key that explains the symbols drawn on the family tree for the chosen condition.

interview.narrativePedigree.keyMayCarry.description: Key row: what the symbol with a horizontal line and a question mark means. condition is the name of the condition the key shows, which the protocol may use.

interview.narrativePedigree.keyMayDevelo.description: Key row: what the symbol with a vertical line and a question mark means. condition is the name of the condition the key shows, which the protocol may use.

interview.narrativePedigree.keyWillDevel.description: Key row: what the symbol with a vertical line means. condition is the name of the condition the key shows, which the protocol may use.

interview.narrativePedigree.showingAll.description: Live announcement when no single condition is selected and the interface shows all protocol conditions.

interview.narrativePedigree.showingCondi.description: Live announcement after selecting a condition. condition is its unchanged protocol-authored name.

interview.narrativePedigree.showingFocus.defaultMessage: Showing {condition}. Focused on {name}. Showing who contributes to their inheritance.

interview.narrativePedigree.statusUnknow.description: Clinical status tooltip and screen-reader label when the inheritance information does not establish a displayed genetic status.

interview.runtime.canvas.description: Announced name of the area where items can be positioned.

interview.runtime.collapseDrawer.description: Accessible action that folds the item tray closed.

interview.runtime.connection.description: Title of the panel for a connection between two people or other items on the canvas, shown when the task gives that kind of connection no name of its own.

interview.runtime.deleteBin.description: Announced name of the drop target that deletes an item.

interview.runtime.drawer.description: Announced name of the tray containing items that can be placed.

interview.runtime.expandDrawer.description: Accessible action that expands the item tray.

interview.runtime.firstNode.description: Fallback accessible name for the first item when its name is missing.

interview.runtime.replaceUnavailableAnsw.description: Button beside an earlier answer that can no longer be shown, which lets the participant type a new answer to replace it.

interview.runtime.secondNode.description: Fallback accessible name for the second item when its name is missing.

interview.runtime.taskErrorDescription.defaultMessage:
# There was an error

There was an error with the interview software, and this task could not be displayed.

Some tasks, such as maps, need an internet connection, so check your connection and then try refreshing the page.
